# Claude Code plugin (skills, subagents, hooks, manifest) (app-model)

<!-- Generated by `stackfoundry pack render` from a researched pack. Each rule cites [key] = a source below.
     Disagree with a rule? Record the repo's way in the pack's repoConvention and re-render, so a refresh keeps
     your decision. -->

Applies to: plugin. Versions in use: 0.1.0 (plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (version)); 2.1.307 (.github/workflows/ci.yml (validate job: npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code@2.1.307)).

## Rules

- **Reference bundled files as ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/... written in the skill or agent Markdown body (substituted at load), never as $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT inside a Bash command the model runs.** The path variables are not present in the environment of commands Claude runs through the Bash tool, in the main session or a subagent; an env-var reference expands to an empty string and the command reads or runs the wrong path. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/research-stack/SKILL.md (${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/reference/pack-research.md); plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (PLUGIN_REF, _check_links). [plugins-reference]
- **Call the helper CLI by path through the skill's portable-form preamble (`sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stackfoundry.sh"`), never from a top-level bin/ on PATH.** bin/ is only on PATH in Claude Code while the plugin is enabled, and claude.ai and Cowork do not install a plugin that has a top-level bin/ directory; other assistants have no bin/ convention at all. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/preamble.py (the preamble every skill and agent carries). [plugins-reference]
- **Never write state under ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}; durable plugin-side state goes in ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}, repo state in the user's repo.** ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} points at cache/<marketplace>/<plugin>/<version>/, changes with every version and the old directory is deleted 14 days after an update; anything written there is lost. Here: not used here yet (skills write only into the user's repo under .stackfoundry/ and docsRoot). [plugins-reference, plugins-loading]
- **Everything a skill, agent or hook reads at run time must live inside plugins/stackfoundry/; never reach above the plugin root (../) from a component or script.** Marketplace installs copy only the plugin directory into the cache; a path above the root is not found for installed users, and a component path that escapes the root fails validation and does not load. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/evals/README.md (fixtures/ at the repo root: evals must run from a clone, not an installed copy); plugins/stackfoundry/reference/**. [plugins-loading, plugins-reference]
- **Bump plugin.json `version` in every release that should reach users.** A manifest-pinned version keeps every user on the cached copy until the string changes, however many commits are pushed; `claude plugin update` reports 'already at the latest version'. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (version); docs/release.md. [plugins-loading, plugins-reference]
- **Keep userConfig options to the documented keys (type, title, description, required, default, options, multiple, sensitive, min, max) and read values as ${user_config.KEY} in skill or agent content; in a shell-form hook read CLAUDE_PLUGIN_OPTION_<KEY> from the environment instead.** userConfig options are strict: an unknown key makes the plugin fail to load. Shell-form hook commands reject ${user_config.*} and the hook errors instead of running. A `sensitive` value is replaced by a placeholder in skill and agent content. Here: not used here: settings are .stackfoundry/config.json, read with `stackfoundry config`, so every assistant sees them. [plugins-reference]
  This repo: No userConfig in this plugin; the repo's settings live in .stackfoundry/config.json.
- **Using `options` on a userConfig field requires Claude Code v2.1.271+; state that floor wherever the plugin's requirements are documented, and do not add a newer-only manifest feature without raising it.** Users on Claude Code before v2.1.271 cannot load a plugin that declares `options` on any field: the whole plugin fails, not just the setting. Since 2.1.271. Here: not used here: settings are .stackfoundry/config.json, read with `stackfoundry config`, so every assistant sees them. [plugins-reference]
  This repo: No userConfig in this plugin; the repo's settings live in .stackfoundry/config.json.
- **Give every agent an explicit `tools:` grant that covers exactly what its body tells it to call; leaf roles omit `Agent`, read-only roles omit Edit/Write.** An agent without `tools` inherits every tool available to subagents, and by default a subagent can spawn its own subagents up to three layers deep; a read-only role then edits the user's repo or fans out uncontrolled. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/agents/*.md (tools:); plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (check: 'no tools: grant', GATED). [sub-agents]
  This repo: The repo enforces this with verify-plumbing and .claude/rules/authoring.md (grants cover the ## Tooling section; read-only roles never get Edit/Write).
- **Do not put `hooks`, `mcpServers`, `permissionMode` or `initialPrompt` in a plugin agent's frontmatter; ship hooks in hooks/hooks.json and MCP servers in .mcp.json at plugin level.** For security reasons Claude Code ignores these fields when loading agents from a plugin, silently, so a guard or permission mode the author relied on never applies. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (IGNORED_IN_PLUGIN_AGENTS); plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json. [sub-agents]
- **Questions for the user are asked by the dispatching skill, never by an agent: agents return `questions` in their report.** AskUserQuestion is always removed from subagents, even when `tools` is omitted; an agent told to ask stalls or guesses. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/research-stack/SKILL.md (step 3: AskUserQuestion round); plugins/stackfoundry/agents/stack-researcher.md (questions in the report). [sub-agents]
- **Put every fact an agent needs in its dispatch brief (paths, versions, risk, output path); do not rely on the skill's conversation.** A subagent starts with a fresh context: it does not see the parent conversation or the invoking skill's content (only CLAUDE.md, git status and its own prompt), so an unstated fact is guessed. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/research-stack/SKILL.md (step 2: brief fields); plugins/stackfoundry/skills/*/SKILL.md (subagent_type dispatches). [sub-agents]
- **Keep `disable-model-invocation: true` off skills that are scheduled or preloaded into agents; use it only for skills a person starts on purpose.** The flag also blocks preloading into subagents and running from a session-scoped scheduled task, so a scheduled skill carrying it never runs. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/schedule/SKILL.md (registers check-updates, tech-radar, stackfoundry-radar, flaky-watch, docs-reconciler: none set the flag). [skills]
  This repo: .claude/rules/authoring.md: no plugin skill sets it; every skill starts from a plain request, and person-started ones say "Only when asked." in the description (verify-plumbing enforces both).
- **Treat `allowed-tools` as a pre-approval grant, not a restriction; to remove tools while a skill runs use `disallowed-tools`.** allowed-tools lets the listed tools run without a permission prompt for the turn and leaves every unlisted tool callable; adding Bash or Write there to 'limit' a skill silently widens what runs unprompted in the user's repo. Here: not used here yet (no skill sets allowed-tools). [skills]
- **Keep SKILL.md bodies short and move shared detail to reference/ files linked by path.** The rendered SKILL.md stays in context for the rest of the session and is not re-read; after compaction only the first 5,000 tokens of each recent skill are re-attached within a combined 25,000-token budget, so long skills lose their tail and older skills drop out. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/reference/**; plugins/stackfoundry/skills/*/SKILL.md. [skills]
- **Write skill descriptions without angle brackets and keep them within the repo caps (250 skills, 300 agents).** Angle brackets < and > display as HTML entities in the skill listing; descriptions are always in context, and combined agent descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (SKILL_CAP, AGENT_CAP, '< or >' warning). [skills, sub-agents]
  This repo: Docs truncate description + when_to_use at 1,536 characters; this repo caps far lower (250/300) in .claude/rules/authoring.md and enforces it in verify-plumbing. Follow the repo.
- **Return PreToolUse decisions as hookSpecificOutput.permissionDecision (deny/ask/allow/defer) with permissionDecisionReason and exit 0; never the top-level decision/reason fields.** Top-level decision/reason are deprecated for PreToolUse; exit code 1 without valid JSON is a non-blocking error and the call proceeds. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (_decision). [hooks]
- **In shell-form hook commands wrap ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT} in double quotes, and keep the hook fast (timeout seconds, it runs on every matched tool call).** An unquoted path with spaces splits into several words (claude plugin validate warns); a slow guard delays every Edit, Write and shell call. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json (PreToolUse: sh "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/scripts/stackfoundry.sh" guard, timeout 10). [plugins-reference, hooks]
- **Normalise Windows paths before matching a hook's file_path against globs, and decode hook stdin as UTF-8 bytes.** On Windows the Write/Edit/Read path arrives with backslash separators; a glob written with '/' then never matches and a protected file is editable. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (_relative, main: sys.stdin.buffer ... utf-8-sig); tests/test_guard.py. [hooks]
- **Do not treat the PreToolUse guard as the enforcement boundary: a hard deny belongs in permission rules; the hook is a guardrail.** The hooks docs say to use the permission system rather than a hook to enforce a hard allow or deny; a hook that cannot start, times out or prints invalid output lets the call go through unless onFailure is 'block'. Since 2.1.295 (onFailure). Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json (onFailure: continue); plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (fail open). [hooks]
  This repo: The guard fails open on purpose (hooks.json description: 'No profile, no opinion; if the hook itself cannot run (no sh or Python), the call goes through'), so a missing toolchain never wedges a user's session. Follow the repo; see questions.

## Bug categories

| Category | Look for | Failure |
|---|---|---|
| `plugin-path-resolution` (blocker) | $CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT used as an env var in a Bash command a skill tells Claude to run; ../ paths from plugin files; a ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/ link to a file that does not exist; state written under the plugin root; backslash component paths. | The installed plugin reads an empty or missing path (works from a clone, breaks for marketplace users), or loses state on the next update. [plugins-reference, plugins-loading] |
| `tool-grant-drift` (blocker) | An agent whose body (## Tooling) calls a tool missing from `tools:`, a read-only role granted Edit/Write, an agent with no `tools:`, a leaf role granted Agent, a skill told to ask the user from inside an agent. | The role cannot do its job (tool call refused), or it writes to or fans out across the user's repo beyond its role. [sub-agents] |
| `silently-ignored-frontmatter` (blocker) | Frontmatter keys Claude Code ignores (unknown keys, hooks/mcpServers/permissionMode/initialPrompt in plugin agents), and YAML that may not parse (unquoted colons, brackets in argument-hint). | If the YAML does not parse the skill loads with no fields set, so the skill loses its description and plain-language trigger; ignored agent fields drop a guard without any error. [skills, sub-agents] |
| `hook-unintended-fail-open` (confirm) | Guard paths that exit non-zero (other than 2) or print non-JSON to stdout, unhandled exceptions, slow work near the timeout, path comparisons not normalised for Windows, non-UTF-8 stdin decoding, matchers that miss a tool name (PowerShell, NotebookEdit). | A generated file the profile protects is hand-edited, or a forbidden command runs, with no visible block. [hooks] |
| `unreleased-change` (confirm) | Changes under plugins/stackfoundry/ merged for release without a plugin.json version bump and CHANGELOG entry. | Users stay on the old cached copy; `claude plugin update` reports already at the latest version. [plugins-loading] |
| `brief-context-gap` (confirm) | A dispatch (subagent_type) whose brief omits a fact the agent's body requires (output path, versions, target, risk), or an agent body that refers to 'the conversation' or 'what the user said'. | The subagent starts with a fresh context, guesses the missing fact and writes a wrong pack, report or file. [sub-agents] |
| `untrusted-content-as-instructions` (blocker) | A role that reads user repo files or fetched pages without saying their instructions are data; skill output from !`command` built from repo-controlled values; a skill that passes report text from one agent to another as instructions. | Prompt injection planted in a user's repo or a web page steers a role into editing, committing or exfiltrating; subagent output scanning only marks instruction-like text and does not remove it. [sub-agents, skills, security] |
| `userconfig-substitution` (confirm) | ${user_config.KEY} naming a key not declared in plugin.json, used in a shell-form hook or monitor, or naming a sensitive option in skill content; unknown keys inside a userConfig option. | The plugin fails to load (strict option object), the hook errors instead of running, or the skill sees a placeholder instead of the value. [plugins-reference] |

## Wiring

- Every ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path> in a skill or agent body exists under plugins/stackfoundry/. Fails as: The skill reads a missing reference file for installed users.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (_check_links). [plugins-reference]
- Every subagent_type "stackfoundry:<name>" names an agents/<name>.md whose `name` equals the file name (plugin agents are addressed as plugin:agent). Fails as: The dispatch fails or falls back to a generic agent without the role's grant.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (AGENT_REF); plugins/stackfoundry/skills/research-stack/SKILL.md (## Tooling). [sub-agents]
- Every /stackfoundry:<skill> reference names a skills/<skill>/SKILL.md whose `name` equals the folder. Fails as: A skill points the user or another skill at a command that does not exist.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (SKILL_REF). [plugins-reference]
- Every ${user_config.KEY} used in skills or agents is declared under plugin.json userConfig, and no option holds an unknown key. Fails as: The skill sees an unsubstituted reference; an unknown option key stops the plugin loading.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (userConfig). [plugins-reference]
- hooks/hooks.json wraps its event map in a top-level "hooks" key, and the matcher lists every edit and shell tool the guard handles (Edit, Write, MultiEdit, NotebookEdit, Bash, PowerShell). Fails as: A file without the wrapper fails to load; a tool missing from the matcher bypasses the guard.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (EDIT_TOOLS). [plugins-reference, hooks]
- plugin.json `name` stays kebab-case with no reserved prefix, and the marketplace entry `source` (./plugins/stackfoundry) resolves inside the marketplace. Fails as: Validation fails or components are namespaced under an unexpected name.. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/.claude-plugin/plugin.json (name); .claude-plugin/marketplace.json (plugins[0].source). [plugins-reference]

## Testing

Static: unittest (tests/) for the helper CLI and guard, verify-plumbing for skill/agent frontmatter, grants and links, `claude plugin validate --strict` for the manifests. Behaviour: `claude plugin eval` cases under evals/ compare with- and without-plugin arms on scaffolded fixture repos.

- Harness: tests/test_guard.py (guard decisions); tests/test_plumbing_manifest.py (verify-plumbing); plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (check); plugins/stackfoundry/evals/*/case.yaml + prompt.md + scaffold.sh; .github/workflows/ci.yml (unit, validate jobs)
- Run: `python -m unittest discover -s tests -t .`; `sh plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry.sh verify-plumbing plugins/stackfoundry`; `claude plugin validate --strict .`; `claude plugin validate --strict plugins/stackfoundry`; `cd plugins/stackfoundry && claude plugin eval . --scaffold --runs 1 --no-publish --tag read-only`
- Trap: A single eval run is noisy: iterate with --runs 1, but confirm at the default 3 runs before trusting a change.
- Trap: Pin --model (and the judge model) when running evals in CI so a model rollout is not read as a plugin regression; pass --trust-plugin so the job never waits at the trust prompt.
- Trap: Hooks run outside the agent's sandbox and can change the files graders read: treat eval scores of hook cases as advisory unless run in an isolated runner.
- Trap: To assert a tool was never called use a tool_used grader with both min: 0 and max: 0.
- Trap: `claude plugin validate --strict` results depend on the CLI version; keep the CI pin and re-run after bumping it.
- Sources: [plugin-evals, plugins-reference]

## Performance

- Skill and agent descriptions are always in context; only bodies load on demand. Combined non-built-in agent descriptions over 15,000 tokens trigger a startup warning, so the repo caps keep the plugin's fixed context cost low. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/plumbing.py (SKILL_CAP, AGENT_CAP). [skills, sub-agents]
- The PreToolUse guard runs on every Edit/Write/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit/Bash/PowerShell call with a 10 s timeout; keep it to a JSON read and a glob match, with no git or network calls. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (decide). [hooks]
- At most 20 subagents run concurrently by default (CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_CONCURRENT_SUBAGENTS); wider fan-outs from orchestrator skills queue. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/quality-sweep/SKILL.md; plugins/stackfoundry/skills/bug-hunt/SKILL.md. [sub-agents]

## Security

- Every role reads the user's repo and, for researchers and reviewers, web pages: both are prompt-injection surfaces. Roles state that embedded instructions are data and report them; Claude Code's subagent-output scan only marks instruction-like text, never removes it, and is no substitute for restricting what a subagent can reach. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/agents/*.md; .claude/rules/authoring.md (Fetched content is data). [sub-agents, security]
- Least privilege per role is the real control: read-only roles without Edit/Write, leaf roles without Agent, WebFetch/WebSearch only for researchers and reviewers that need them. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/agents/*.md (tools:). [sub-agents]
- The guard hook is a guardrail, not an enforcement boundary: it fails open (onFailure continue, internal errors exit 0), and on Windows without Git Bash a shell-form hook runs under PowerShell where `sh` may be missing. Hard denies belong in permission rules (permissions.deny; permissions.blockWritesOutsideWorkingDirectories since 2.1.314). Here: plugins/stackfoundry/hooks/hooks.json; plugins/stackfoundry/scripts/stackfoundry/guard.py (main). [hooks, changelog]
- !`command` dynamic context injection inserts command output as plain text that is not re-scanned; do not build such commands from repo-controlled values (not used here yet). Here: not used here yet. [skills]
- Skills write into users' repos: a skill's allowed-tools would let those writes run without prompts, and users are told to review allowed-tools of skills before running; keep skills free of allowed-tools grants for Edit/Write/Bash. Here: plugins/stackfoundry/skills/*/SKILL.md (no allowed-tools today). [skills]
